claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own measurements. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure, and the trace measures 30.89 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against the platform's optimal estimate of 22.10 km stored on the trip record. Excess = 8.79 km, or 39.8% of optimal. Both establishment gates in POL-RD-01 pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, so no threshold straddle is in play here and the trace figure is the one cited.

The excess is additionally a MATERIAL deviation under POL-RD-01: 8.79 km exceeds the 8.0 km absolute materiality gate. The two limbs of the materiality test are alternatives, so the fact that 39.8% falls short of the 50% limb does not matter. Materiality is what triggers the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check, and it is assessed on the excess remaining after any POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 adjustment — none of which is available to the driver here.

The trip record's 30.9 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test; the trace's 30.89 km governs under POL-RD-01. Nothing outcome-changing turns on the difference in this case, because both figures clear both gates, but the correct excess denominator is the trace figure and the correct excess is 8.79 km, not the 8.8 km the rounded field would suggest.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes and needs no corroboration. It carries 217 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100% coverage, an empty gaps array, a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds and a sustained sampling interval of 10 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and no sampling interval above 30 seconds — so the trace carries the establishment finding on its own and no escalation arises under POL-RD-10(3).

The driver's fog explanation is unsupported by anything in the pool. POL-RD-03 exonerates a deviation only against a traffic_advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and is matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor. No such advisory exists: EV-ADVIS-00505-01 is MISSING, its payload is null, and it carries admissibility weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING, detail: no advisory covers the SLE or TPE in this window). I disclose that impairment expressly: this artifact can prove nothing by its content, but its absence is itself citable, and it leaves condition (a) of POL-RD-03 unmet, so the clause cannot exonerate the 8.79 km.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden and it has shifted to the driver. Trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00505; the trace runs from the recorded start at 05:46:40 to the recorded end at 06:22:40 with no timestamp disagreement, and the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The driver must therefore point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. His counterparty statement does not deny the route — it explains it ('I went around') — and its reason is a fog assertion naming no traffic_advisory ID, no closed road and no gantry. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge that burden, and assertions citing no evidence ID carry no weight.

No rider-requested detour can be made out under POL-RD-04. The chat log for this trip contains 0 messages, with first_message_at and last_message_at both null and message_count 0, so there is no rider instruction, no timestamp to test against the departure from the optimal corridor, no named road, and no waypoint_hint field for the 200 m corroboration test. The clause's corroboration limb is not even reachable, and POL-RD-04 offers the driver no exoneration.

POL-RD-05 cannot be run. Pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null with them. There is therefore no stored re-quote against which POL-RD-01 could be re-applied between amended endpoints, and no basis for substituting any other optimal figure. The dropoff label ('Changi Airport Terminal 1, Arrival Pick-up Bay 3') carries venue_id null and sits under an amendment field the record never stamped; the clause requires an amendment, not an amended-sounding bay label.

The pooled-itinerary baseline in POL-RD-12 does not apply. The vehicle type on this trip is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the 22.10 km figure is the ordinary platform optimal computed at booking and is the correct comparator under POL-RD-01. There is no matched-itinerary optimal for the driver to point to, and no co-rider distance to exclude.

With the deviation established and no exculpatory clause available, the refund is arithmetic rather than discretionary. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not displace POL-RD-02. Recomputing on the recorded components: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.10 km + 0.28 x 27.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls on the optimal route + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time fee - 0 promo discount = 28.735 recomputed fare. Against charged_total of 37.86, the refund before rounding is 9.1250, which rounds UP to SGD 9.15 payable.

The refund is a partial, not a full, refund. 9.15 is 24.1% of the 37.86 charged, far below the 90% share that would convert the award into a FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-02, so the correct outcome value is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15. The figure is also well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no de minimis disposal is available to the driver.

On the profile check POL-RD-06 requires after a material finding, the rider does not press the limb (b) uplift, because the clause's own fields do not support it: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0.00 — below both the 3-flag limb and the 0.05-ratio limb alongside the 40-trip minimum. The rider equally does not rely on driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags: that is a lifetime counter, not the trailing-90-day figure the clause names, and POL-GEN-01 makes it context only. I state this so the record shows the check was run and the uplift is not being manufactured.

No mandatory-escalation trigger in POL-RD-10 fires, and this case should be decided rather than held. Trigger (2): the trip identifier is TRP-00505 on all three artifacts. Trigger (3): the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07, so there is nothing requiring corroboration. Trigger (4): the first and last fixes sit exactly on the recorded start and end times, so no timestamps disagree or run backwards. Trigger (6): 9.15 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total. Trigger (7): there is no admissible contradictory evidence of comparable strength at all — a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 carries no fact under POL-GEN-02, so the driver's fog account is not 'evidence' in the sense that limb means. Trigger (5) is not engaged either: the driver's assertion cites no artifact against which an exculpatory clause could be invoked, and a missing advisory is a citable absence that leaves his burden undischarged, not a data failure that converts a proven rider claim into a held file.

The driver's 4.86 rating, 1,000-day account age and 1,700 lifetime trips are on his profile, and his statement leans on his general reliability as a professional, but under POL-GEN-01 those fields are CONTEXT ONLY: no profile field may establish a fact about this trip or defeat a finding built on this trip's own trace. They cannot rebut an 8.79 km excess measured on this trip's GPS. The rider also asks the tribunal not to reason from the rider's profile in the other direction: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is nowhere near engaged and this claim needs no corroboration beyond the trace.

No pass-through correction arises under POL-RD-09 and none is claimed, which keeps the arithmetic honest: erp_gantries is empty, the off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, and the airport surcharge line is 0.00 — correctly so, because a surcharge applies to trips ORIGINATING at an airport and this trip ENDS at one. There is therefore no off-route ERP to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure (POL-RD-09(1) forbids that double count) and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) on these lines.

The rider does not press the SGD 210 rebooking cost or the missed check-in as a ground of decision. No clause in the loaded policy converts a missed flight into a refundable line, and the fare breakdown contains no such line; the remedy the policy provides is the arithmetic refund of the disputed charge under POL-RD-02, and POL-GEN-03 fixes the vocabulary in which that remedy is expressed as a refund to the filing party. The rider's recorded contested amount is the SGD 37.86 charged on the fare breakdown, and that is the sum the ruling should move.

claims.text: The rider's demand for the SGD 210 airline rebooking fee has no home in this policy. A route-deviation ruling moves money only through the POL-RD-02 fare recomputation and standalone POL-RD-09 pass-through corrections, and POL-GEN-03 defines the sole amounts a ruling may carry - a refund to the filing party and, on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling, a driver payment. Consequential loss such as a missed check-in is not a remedy this policy provides, and no artifact in this pool evidences the flight, the rebooking or what it cost; the contested sum is bounded by the fare ledger, whose charged_total is SGD 37.86.

No repeat-deviation uplift is available against this driver. His driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, a ratio of 0.00, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 pattern test is met - the count is below 3 and the ratio is far below 0.05. It follows that the FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is not triggered; under POL-GEN-01 only those two trailing-90-day fields may ground this test, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter on the same artifact is not the field POL-RD-06 names.

The driver's fog and route-around defence cannot be run on this record. The only traffic advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00505-01, is MISSING - it has no payload, carries weight 0.0 and fires issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, its own note recording that no advisory covers the SLE or TPE in this window - so POL-RD-03 limbs (a) to (c) cannot be satisfied and the driver cannot discharge the burden that POL-RD-08 shifts to him once the rider has shown a qualifying excess on an unimpaired trace. I do not present the absence as clean evidence: it is an absence, at weight 0.0, and it is citable as such.

Because the driver's exculpatory clause is asserted with no traffic advisory covering the trip window, POL-RD-10(5) is engaged: a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory is that clause's own worked example. The advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00505-01 is in the pool but carries no payload at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it neither names a road the optimal route traverses nor bears a validity window overlapping the trip. Escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal - it replaces the ruling, no monetary outcome issues, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded - which is the correct disposition of a defence the record cannot test either way.

Nothing may be added on top of the fare arithmetic. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP gantry lines, zero tolls and a zero airport surcharge - correctly so, since the surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at Changi and this trip ENDS there - so POL-RD-09 yields no standalone pass-through refund, no billing-integrity failure arises under POL-RD-09(4), and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting any such line twice on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

In the alternative, if this case is ruled on the money rather than escalated, the rider's fare remedy cannot exceed the POL-RD-02 partial. On a recomputed fare of SGD 28.735 against a charged_total of SGD 37.86 the refund is SGD 9.125, payable rounded up to SGD 9.15, which is 24.1% of the amount charged - far below the 90% share that would convert it to FULL_REFUND and comfortably above the SGD 0.50 de minimis - and with the POL-RD-06 uplift closed by this driver's clean 90-day record there is no route to a full refund of the fare, let alone to the rebooking sum.
